background.source: Dream of the Red Chamber, also known as The Story of the Stone, is a masterpiece novel composed by Cao Xueqin in the middle of the 18th century. The novel is regarded as one of the Four Great Classical Novels of Chinese literature which depicts the rise and decline of a family much alike to Cao's own and, by extension, of the dynasty itself. It offers a deep insight into the worldview, aesthetics, life-styles, and social relations of 18th-century China. Exploring a range of philosophical and religious questions, the novel's intricate plot delves into the concepts of family honor and official power. At its core, the novel is a memorial to the women that Cao Xueqin knew in his youth, including friends, relatives, and servants. While the author depicts the power of the father over the family, the novel provides a profound portrayal of women's lives in this era. The story centers around Jia Baoyu, Lin Daiyu, Shi Xiangyun, and other members of the Jia clan as they navigate their personal relationships and family dynamics. The novel was not published until nearly three decades after Cao's death when it was edited by Gao E and Cheng Weiyuan, adding 40 chapters, to become the most widely circulated version. The novel has been translated into different titles, including A Dream of Red Mansions, Red Chamber Dream, and The Story of the Stone.

His contributions to the country have been recognized by his appointment as an alternate member of the 16th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party. 

Despite being a man of great accomplishments, Nie Haihua has also shown a keen interest in women's destiny and social morality. This is clearly evidenced in his appreciation of legendary figures such as Yan Ling, Cui Yingying, and Zhao Feiyan, who have become symbols of femininity and strength. Overall, Nie Haihua's career and values are a testament to his commitment to the betterment of China and its people.
